title: scGR-seq: Integrated analysis of glycan and RNA in single cells
author: Odaka, Ozaki, et al.
materials: Nextera XT DNA Library Preparation Kit

steps.title: Wash Sepharose CL-4B gel
steps.instruction: Wash 20 g of Sepharose CL-4B gel using a glass filter in 500 mL of Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Epoxy‑activate Sepharose resin
steps.instruction: Suspend the washed Sepharose CL-4B gel in 30 mL of Milli‑Q water, add 3 mL epichlorohydrin and 13 mL of 2 N NaOH, and incubate at 40 °C for 2 h with shaking.

steps.title: Wash epoxy‑activated resin
steps.instruction: Wash the epoxy‑activated Sepharose CL-4B with 500 mL of Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Couple sugar ligands to resin
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mmol of sugar ligands (see Table 1) in 80 mL of 0.1 M NaOH (pH 13.0), mix with the epoxy‑activated Sepharose, incubate at 40 °C for 24 h, then wash with 500 mL of Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Block excess epoxy groups
steps.instruction: Resuspend the sugar‑immobilized Sepharose CL-4B in 50 mL of 1 M monoethanolamine (pH 8.0) and incubate at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Wash blocked resin
steps.instruction: Wash the resin with 0.1 M acetate buffer (pH 4.0) containing 0.5 M NaCl, then with 0.1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0) containing 0.5 M NaCl.

steps.title: Resuspend and store resin
steps.instruction: Resuspend the sugar‑immobilized Sepharose CL-4B in Milli‑Q water and store at 4 °C until further use.

steps.title: Pack resin into micro column
steps.instruction: Pack 1 mL of the sugar‑immobilized Sepharose CL-4B into Micro Bio‑Spin chromatography columns and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Equilibrate column with PBSE
steps.instruction: Wash the 1 mL sugar‑immobilized Sepharose CL-4B column with 1 mL PBSE at 4 °C.

steps.title: Load DNA‑barcoded lectin
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of PBSE to the DNA‑barcoded lectin solution, apply onto the column, and collect the 100 µL flow‑through fraction.

steps.title: Wash column with PBSE
steps.instruction: Wash the column three times with 400 µL PBSE each; collect each 400 µL wash fraction.

steps.title: Elute lectin with specific sugar
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL of PBSE containing the appropriate sugar for each lectin (see Table 1) to the column, repeat three times, and collect each 400 µL elution fraction.

steps.title: Prepare SDS‑PAGE samples
steps.instruction: Mix 4 µL of each fraction (lectin only, flow‑through, wash, elution) with 4 µL SDS sample buffer.

steps.title: Load samples onto SDS‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Load 8 µL of each prepared sample and 5 µL of prestained protein size marker onto a 17 % SDS‑PAGE gel.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Run the gel in SDS running buffer at 100 V for 20 min.

steps.title: Stain gel with GelRed
steps.instruction: Stain the gel with GelRed according to the manufacturer’s protocol (stains free DNA and lectin‑conjugated DNA barcodes).

steps.title: Stain gel with silver
steps.instruction: After GelRed staining, stain the same gel with silver‑staining reagents following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Dialyze elution fractions
steps.instruction: Dialyze the recovered elution fractions against 0.1× PBS using a Tube‑O‑Dialyzer, Medi 8 kDa.

steps.title: Concentrate purified lectins
steps.instruction: Concentrate the dialyzed lectins using an Amicon Ultra 0.5 mL centrifugal filter (10 kDa MWCO).

steps.title: Quantify protein and DNA
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration by Bradford assay and DNA concentration by Quant‑iT OliGreen ssDNA kit; calculate the DNA‑to‑lectin ratio.

steps.title: Prepare DNA‑barcoded probe mix
steps.instruction: Mix 41 DNA‑barcoded probes (final 5 µg/mL for each lectin) in a 1.5 mL tube and bring volume to 100 µL with PBS/BSA.

steps.title: Store probe mixture
steps.instruction: Store the probe mixture at –30 °C.

steps.title: Coat plate with Matrigel
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL Matrigel to each well of a 6‑well plate and incubate at room temperature for 1 h.

steps.title: Thaw medium and plate hiPSCs
steps.instruction: Thaw mTeSR Plus medium at 37 °C for 5–15 min, then plate the appropriate number of 201B7 hiPSCs into each well containing 2 mL of the medium.

steps.title: Incubate hiPSCs
steps.instruction: Culture the cells for 2–3 days in a CO₂ incubator set to 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Dissociate and resuspend hiPSCs
steps.instruction: Recover the cells with gentle cell dissociation reagent and resuspend in mTeSR Plus medium supplemented with 10 µM Y‑27632.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for using human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and hiPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs). However, we have also used this protocol in other cells, such as human dermal fibroblasts, hiPSC-derived neurons, and several cell lines. This protocol consists of three major steps (Figure 1)-Figure 1Schematic diagram of scGlycan/RNA sequencing(A) Illustration of the DNA-barcoded lectin.(B) Schematic illustration of scGlycan-seq, scRNA-seq, and scGR-seq. Figure reprinted with permission from Minoshima et al. (2021). (i) Single cell Glycan-seq (scGlycan-seq) (ii) Single cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) (iii) Integrated data analysis (scGR-seq) Standard cell culture procedures and humidified incubators are required for the maintenance of cell culture. For scRNA-seq, we use RamDA-seq, a plate-based single-cell total RNA sequencing method (Hayashi et al., 2018). We use the next-generation sequencer, MiSeq (Illumina) and the barcode DNA counting system (Minoshima et al., 2021) to count DNA-barcodes derived from each lectin.
